paragraphs.text: Kruer syndrome is a neurodevelopmental disorder caused by a recurrent de novo heterozygous FBXO31 mutation. Its core features are cerebral palsy with mixed hypotonia, spasticity and dystonia; global developmental delay or intellectual disability; and speech impairment. Some patients also have neuropsychiatric features and abnormalities of the corpus callosum and white matter (Galaz-Montoya et al., 2026). Dzinovic et al. (2021) suggested that emerging hallmarks of FBXO31-related disease included delayed psychomotor development, pyramidal and extrapyramidal dysfunction (spasticity and dystonia), impaired expressive and receptive language, and intellectual disability.

paragraphs.text: Dzinovic et al. (2021) reported a 9-year-old Slovakian boy, born to nonconsanguineous parents, with a complex, nonprogressive movement disorder syndrome dominated by spasticity and dystonia, with onset in the first months of life. He had neonatal muscular hypotonia and global developmental delay. He lost speech at 18 months of age and had absent expressive language and a receptive language disorder. He had generalized dystonia of the arms, legs and trunk. Signs of pyramidal tract dysfunction included spasticity, which was worse in the legs than the arms, hyperreflexia, and clonus in both legs. He walked with an unsteady spastic-dystonic gait, had reduced manual dexterity, and had moderate intellectual disability. He was diagnosed with spastic-dystonic cerebral palsy. Brain MRI showed reduced parietal and occipital white matter volume and global white matter dysmyelination. Blood and urine lactate were slightly elevated on one occasion. He had no distinctive craniofacial features, behavioral abnormalities, or congenital malformations. Dzinovic et al. (2021) compared him with the 2 patients reported by Jin et al. (2020). All 3 had motor and/or speech delay, mild to moderate intellectual disability, abnormal speech, and spasticity that mainly affected the lower limbs and led to a diagnosis of cerebral palsy. Dystonia was seen only in their patient.

paragraphs.text: Galaz-Montoya et al. (2026) studied 7 unrelated probands with the recurrent FBXO31 mutation. They re-evaluated 3 previously published cases and found 4 more probands through advocacy networks, GeneMatcher, and clinician referral. The core neurodevelopmental profile was cerebral palsy (mixed hypotonia, spasticity, and dystonia), global developmental delay/intellectual disability, and speech impairment. Neuropsychiatric features were sometimes prominent and included attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, anxiety, stereotypies, autistic features, and behavioral dysregulation. Neuroimaging often showed a hypoplastic corpus callosum and posterior-predominant white matter changes, and 1 individual had gray matter heterotopias. The authors also described a subtle, consistent facial gestalt.

paragraphs.text: Jin et al. (2020) performed whole-exome sequencing in 250 parent-offspring trios with cerebral palsy. In 2 unrelated patients with spastic diplegic cerebral palsy (F218 and F699), they identified the same de novo heterozygous missense mutation in the FBXO31 gene, D334N. Sanger sequencing of the probands and their parents confirmed de novo occurrence. The authors considered this identical de novo variant in 2 unrelated patients unlikely to have occurred by chance, and identified FBXO31 as a novel monogenic cause of cerebral palsy. The D334N variant affected a conserved residue within the cyclin D1-binding pocket. Patient fibroblasts had lower cyclin D levels than controls, consistent with an apparent gain of function in cyclin D degradation.

paragraphs.text: In a 9-year-old Slovakian boy with Kruer syndrome, Dzinovic et al. (2021) used trio whole-exome sequencing to identify a de novo heterozygous c.1000G-A transition in the FBXO31 gene, resulting in an asp334-to-asn (D334N) substitution. The variant was absent from both healthy parents and from control databases. It changed a conserved residue in a domain that interacts with the FBXO31 substrate cyclin D1. The authors classified it as pathogenic under ACMG guidelines and found no other potentially disease-relevant variants in the exome.

paragraphs.text: In 2 unrelated patients with Kruer syndrome who had spastic diplegic cerebral palsy, intellectual disability, expressive language disorder, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, Jin et al. (2020) identified a de novo heterozygous asp334-to-asn (D334N) mutation in the FBXO31 gene. The mutation was found by whole-exome sequencing of parent-offspring trios, and de novo occurrence was confirmed by Sanger sequencing. The residue is conserved and lies within the cyclin D1-binding pocket. Patient fibroblasts had lower cyclin D levels than controls, consistent with an apparent gain of function.

checks.claim: Jin et al. (2020) identified a de novo heterozygous asp334-to-asn (D334N) mutation in the FBXO31 gene in 2 unrelated patients with Kruer syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: We also identified two unrelated cases with an identical DNM (encoding p.Asp334Asn; Fig. 2a and Supplementary Table 4) in FBXO31
checks.explanation: Variant and patients supported; paper describes them as cerebral palsy cases, not 'Kruer syndrome'.

checks.claim: The 2 unrelated patients with the FBXO31 D334N mutation reported by Jin et al. (2020) had spastic diplegic cerebral palsy, intellectual disability, expressive language disorder, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Both patients in our cohort exhibited spastic diplegic CP (Supplementary Table 4 and Supplementary Videos F218 and F699), ID, expressive language disorder and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.

checks.claim: Jin et al. (2020) found the FBXO31 D334N mutation by whole-exome sequencing of parent-offspring trios.
checks.evidence_quote: We performed whole-exome sequencing of 250 parent-offspring trios, and observed enrichment of damaging de novo mutations in cerebral palsy cases.

checks.claim: De novo occurrence of the FBXO31 D334N mutation in the patients reported by Jin et al. (2020) was confirmed by Sanger sequencing.
checks.evidence_quote: Sanger traces of the mother, father and proband from families F218 and F699 verify de novo inheritance and the position of the variant (red arrow).

checks.claim: FBXO31 residue asp334 is conserved.
checks.evidence_quote: Asp334 is a conserved residue within the binding pocket on FBXO31

checks.claim: FBXO31 residue asp334 lies within the cyclin D1-binding pocket.
checks.evidence_quote: D334 is positioned around the cyclin D1 (green)-binding pocket on FbXO31.

checks.claim: Fibroblasts from patients with the FBXO31 D334N mutation had lower cyclin D levels than controls, consistent with an apparent gain of function.
checks.evidence_quote: FBXO31 p.Asp334Asn affects the cyclin D interaction site (Fig. 2b), leading to an apparent gain of function of cyclin D degradation (Fig. 2c).
checks.explanation: Reduced cyclin D in patient fibroblasts, interpreted as apparent gain of function.

paragraphs.text: In a 9-year-old Slovakian boy with spastic-dystonic cerebral palsy, moderate intellectual disability, and absent expressive language, Dzinovic et al. (2021) identified a de novo heterozygous c.1000G-A transition in the FBXO31 gene, resulting in an asp334-to-asn (D334N) substitution. The mutation was found by trio whole-exome sequencing and was absent from both healthy parents and from control databases.

checks.claim: Dzinovic et al. (2021) identified a de novo heterozygous c.1000G-A transition in the FBXO31 gene, resulting in an asp334-to-asn (D334N) substitution, in a 9-year-old Slovakian boy.
checks.evidence_quote: the proband was heterozygous for a FBXO31 c.1000G > A (p. Asp334Asn) missense substitution, which had occurred de novo
checks.explanation: Stated directly; proband is a 9-year-old Slovakian boy.

checks.claim: The 9-year-old Slovakian boy with the FBXO31 D334N mutation reported by Dzinovic et al. (2021) had spastic-dystonic cerebral palsy, moderate intellectual disability, and absent expressive language.
checks.evidence_quote: Diagnosis of cerebral palsy (CP) | Yes (spastic‐dystonic CP)
checks.explanation: Table also lists moderate ID; text states no expressive language.

checks.claim: Dzinovic et al. (2021) found the FBXO31 c.1000G-A mutation by trio whole-exome sequencing.
checks.evidence_quote: the proband and his parents underwent trio‐WES in a research context

checks.claim: The FBXO31 c.1000G-A mutation reported by Dzinovic et al. (2021) was absent from both healthy parents and from control databases.
checks.evidence_quote: This variant, absent from control databases (gnomAD, in‐house exomes)
checks.explanation: Absent from controls; de novo status implies absence from healthy parents.

paragraphs.text: Galaz-Montoya et al. (2026) found the recurrent de novo heterozygous D334N mutation in 7 unrelated probands with Kruer syndrome, 3 previously published and 4 newly ascertained.

checks.claim: Galaz-Montoya et al. (2026) found the recurrent de novo heterozygous FBXO31 D334N mutation in 7 unrelated probands with Kruer syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: All seven individuals carried the recurrent de novo FBXO31 p.Asp334Asn variant.
checks.explanation: The abstract confirms seven individuals with the de novo variant but does not say they are unrelated.

checks.claim: Of the 7 probands with the FBXO31 D334N mutation studied by Galaz-Montoya et al. (2026), 3 were previously published and 4 were newly ascertained.
checks.evidence_quote: we re-evaluated three published cases and ascertained four additional probands
